stagedNote: STAGED ONLY, not ingested. Dry-plan via lib/insert-set-key.cjs planFile() now PASSES (separate=[], foldRungs={}) after the R67 roster fix below. The repo already carries a disjoint 3-rung ladder file for this same product at backend/data/checklists/scraped/acq-2026-09-15-ladders/2026-topps-baseball-ladder.csv (checklistinsider source, Sandglitter Gold/75 Years of Topps/Base Confetti) -- this Beckett file's 7 originally-stated parallel rungs (Golden Mirror/Golden Mirror Legend/Vintage Stock/True Photo/Player Number/Team Color Border/1952 Topps Rookie Variation) do not overlap it at all; combined they are 10 distinct rungs, zero collisions between the two sources.

rookieCardFlag.rule: Beckett's xlsx appends an ' RC' rookie-card flag to the player field on the sheets that carry it (the Base sheet, and the Golden Mirror Variation section which lives on a sheet with the same column layout) -- never on the sheets for the other 8 stated parallel rungs or the 7 originally-own-cards sections. The checklist-csv-contract (docs/reference/checklist-csv-contract.md) has no rookie/RC column, so a new one was NOT invented. The ' RC' suffix is stripped from every `player` cell in this CSV instead, and the fact is preserved here as a card-level list rather than a per-row column, since RC is a property of the CARD, not of one parallel's spelling of it.
rookieCardFlag.whyItMatters: cleanPlayerName (backend/src/services/portfolioiq/cardCatalog.service.ts) has no RC handling -- confirmed by running it directly: cleanPlayerName('Jonah Tong RC') returns 'Jonah Tong RC' unchanged, and playerSlugify() on that mints `jonah-tong-rc` while every other row for the same player (all 8 other parallels of card #4, every sale, every other product) mints `jonah-tong`. Left unstripped, base rows would never match on playerSlug against their own parallels or against sales for the same card.
rookieCardFlag.measured: 142 rows carried the suffix pre-strip: 71 plain-base rows (category=base, blank parallel) + 71 Golden Mirror Variation rows (the one parallel rung that shares the Base sheet's column layout) -- the same 71 distinct cardNumbers in both groups, 0 exceptions. Every other stated parallel and every one of the 7 roster-folded sections below already read the plain name with no RC suffix anywhere.

r67RosterFold.rule: convertBeckettChecklistXlsx.cjs's classifySections only folds a section onto Base via title-containment (extendsName) or FINISH_WORD vocabulary. 7 sections shared no name tokens with 'Base Set' and are not FINISH_WORD spellings, so they never became fold candidates and stayed category=insert-<slug>/auto-<slug> with a blank parallel column -- which put them on a same-numbered collision course with base at the plain product key, and lib/insert-set-key.cjs's planFile() refused the raw conversion on 7 unregistered same-numbered keys. Re-derived by hand applying R67's own roster test: for each refused section, compare its (cardNumber -> player) map against Base Set (category=base, blank parallel) on the numbers they share, players normalised (split on '/', trim, lowercase, de-duplicate, sort), AFTER the RC-suffix strip above. A section whose roster equals or is a subset of base's on every shared number, zero disagreements, folds onto base with the section's own header text as the parallel (isAuto is untouched -- a signed section stays signed). A section with a disagreement, or its own numbering the parent lacks, keeps its own category. This exact rule is what backend/scripts/convertBeckettChecklistXlsx.cjs is being taught in the companion PR (see below); this manifest is the byte-for-byte evidence trail for the hand-applied version that produced the CSV committed here BEFORE that PR existed.
r67RosterFold.originalConverterOutput: NOT kept as a sibling file in this directory -- ingest-checklist-csv-to-catalog.cjs sweeps every *.csv in a directory (fs.readdirSync(DIR).filter(n => n.endsWith('.csv'))), so a second CSV here would be ingested alongside this one the first time this directory is pointed at that script. The full per-row evidence is this manifest section instead; the original converter run is reproducible from the source xlsx (sourceUrl above) with `node backend/scripts/convertBeckettChecklistXlsx.cjs --xlsx <file> --year 2026 --set-key topps --sport baseball --set-name "2026 Topps Series 1 Baseball"` before the classifySections fix in the companion PR lands, or byte-identically reproducible by that PR's own fixture test after it lands.
